text:
Devon: Heads up — after the kernel-selection rollback yesterday we're seeing a subtle p95 regression on streaming endpoints. p50 ok, but p95 up ~40ms on long chat sessions. anyone else?
Anita: saw this in dashboards too. appears correlated with chunksize changes + the new fused-attn path. :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the config used for the canary? microbatch size, chunk/flush intervals, kernel hint?
Devon: Canary config snippet: `microbatch=4`, `chunk_tokens=8`, `flush_ms=40`, kernel hints: prefer="fused-attn, triton-matmul". rollout was 10% to prod.
Kai: perf-bot traces show higher tail for streams where KV cache miss rate spikes. could be extra memcpy in the new kernel path.
perf-bot: @channel automated profile attached: cold-starts excluded, sample=2k requests. :robot_face:
perf-bot: ```
hot path time breakdown (median):
  token_emit: 3.8ms
  attention_fused_kernel: 12.2ms
  matmul_triton: 6.1ms
  kv_cache_copy: 9.4ms
  serialization+net: 2.5ms
hot path p95: token_emit 9.6ms, kv_cache_copy 23.1ms, fused_kernel 34.8ms
```
Anita: kv_cache_copy at p95=23ms is worrying — that almost doubles perceived latency when streaming chunks are small and frequent.
Sam: hypothesis: fused-attn reduces avg kernel time but forces a different KV layout that triggers more copies for streaming with non-consecutive prefixes. So throughput up but tail suffers.
Devon: yes that matches. p50 improves slightly but p95 regresses. Our SLO is p95 token latency 100ms. some customers flirting with it.
Kai: quick experiment idea: increase `chunk_tokens` to 16 and bump `flush_ms` to 80 for streams with long contexts. That will reduce number of KV syncs and amortize memcpy. tradeoff: slightly higher first-token latency.
Anita: can we do an A/B: keep new kernels but route 20% of long-session traffic to bigger-chunk policy and compare p95/p99?
Sam: agree. Also want low-level trace of memcpy calls. Add `KV_COPY=trace` in runtime env to log sizes.
Devon: Will run two canaries: (A) chunk=8 flush=40 (current), (B) chunk=16 flush=80, both with fused kernel. Collect p50/p95/p99 + tokens/s + cost delta.
perf-bot: scheduled canaries: A 10% (existing), B 10% new. start 2026-03-18T15:10Z.
Kai: another angle: kernel selection policy could pick a tiled-matmul for long sequences which keeps KV layout compatible with old path — less copies. We should add a rule: if session_length>512 prefer tiled-matmul.
Anita: yes but confirm throughput impact. Might increase GPU time per token and blow up bill. Need cost/latency curve.
Sam: I profiled matmul_tiled vs fused for long seqs: fused: 25% faster avg, tiled: 15% faster p95. So tiled is safer for SLO-sensitive workloads.
Devon: action list:
- Run canary B and gather p50/p95/p99 and KV_COPY logs (Sam)
- Add memtrace on 1% traffic to confirm copy counts (Kai)
- Eval cost delta for tiled-matmul fallback and propose policy (Anita)
- If B reduces p95 by >20ms and cost delta <8% -> roll to 50% (Devon)
Anita: also add a short-term mitigation: per-route override in console to set chunk_tokens/flush_ms so customers can opt-in to lower perceived latency.
Sam: nit: instrument perceived-latency metric in frontend (time to first token + inter-token gap P95) so product sees impact.
Devon: good call. I'll file a quick ticket and ping support to notify affected customers if we breach SLO.
Kai: for the canary, include the profiling flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/runs/1968001234/flame (will capture copy hotspots).
Devon: thanks all. let's reconvene after 2h when canary has 5k requests. :thumbsup: 
Anita: :eyes:
Sam: adding the experiment commands here: ```bash
# run streaming benchmark
./bench_stream --model redwood-13b --concurrency 64 --session_len 800 --chunk_tokens 16 --flush_ms 80 --profile=flame
```
Kai: if anyone sees sudden p99 spikes while canary is on, abort and rollback to prior kernel immediately.
Devon: noted. I'll keep a watch and set automated abort at +40ms p95 over baseline.
perf-bot: canary started; will post interim metrics at +30m and +2h.
